text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Two contracts have been signed with companies to prospect for gold east of Aswan and in Sinai...and negotiations are being made with other firms to extract iron. The gold contracts were signed with a Canadian firm.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak wins the Nehru award.
- United States, Egypt and the European Union coordinate their positions to restart peace talks.
- French defence minister begins official visit to Egypt.

- Agricultural credit banks to grant tenant farmers soft loans to enable them to buy agricultural land. The cost of the land will be paid in installments over 10 years. The state has initially set aside 1,750 acres (708 hectares) for this scheme.

- Mubarak receives telephone calls from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad to discuss the latest developments in the Middle East. Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh and the president of the United Arab Emirates, Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, also telephone Mubarak on the anniversary of the July 23, 1952 revolution.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri's cabinet will discuss international offers to set up factories, farms and companies in the New Valley and Sinai.
- President decress that there be tumour treatment centres in the governorates.
- An Egyptian-American plan to resume peace talks.
- Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar says the youth must bear some of the responsibility of developing their nation.
